more.p: No page the research opened says the J4580 blocks or nags about third-party 901 cartridges. A 2017 article on HP firmware that blocked non-HP cartridges names other OfficeJet models, not the OfficeJet 4500 or J4580. Compatible 901 cartridges are on sale in Israel (zap.co.il).

Windows 10 and 11 print through the Windows built-in driver, and a few owners got HP's full package working on Windows 11, but HP's J4580 page usually lists no Windows 11 driver and scanning on Windows 11 failed for at least one owner in May 2026 with no fix found.

more.label: Driver
more.p: Windows built-in (basic) driver for printing, which HP's own Windows 10 guidance (quoted by a volunteer in January 2023) points to. For full features, owners use a download from HP's J4500 Series or J4580 software page, which volunteers link as 'Officejet J4580 - driver software - Windows'; one owner reports it worked on Windows 11 in May 2026, another reports scanning still not recognised with it. An April 2025 HP Support reply says the full package on Windows 11 covers printing, scanning and faxing (no owner confirmed that).

more.label: App required
more.p: optional

more.label: Known problems
items: No Windows 11 full driver on HP's J4580 page in threads from 2022 to 2024 (no fix in those threads; a volunteer download link was offered, and one 2026 owner says it installed)
Windows 11 says 'Officejet J4500 Series driver is unavailable' under Bluetooth and devices (fixed for one owner in May 2026 by installing the volunteer-linked driver; thread 9650149)
Scanner not recognised on a new Windows 11 laptop that prints fine, even after the volunteer driver (no fix found; owner gave up in May 2026; thread 9651955)
HP Scan Doctor says the full software is not installed, so scanning fails (fixed for one owner in January 2022 by a community instruction the owner followed; thread 8258748)
Fax on Windows 11: no page read says it works; the built-in driver covers printing and scanning only (not verified)

more.label: Scanning
more.p: The device has a flatbed scanner with a 20-sheet document feeder. On Windows 11, owners have scanned with HP's full package, but in May 2026 a new Windows 11 laptop did not see the scanner even though it printed; HP's built-in-driver guidance points to the Windows Fax and Scan, Paint or Windows Scan apps, and no owner confirmed that route for this model.
Only two owner-opinion pages could be read (eBay UK's 12 reviews and a small Russian reader poll), which is below the three-source minimum, so the star score is reported but not rated.

more.p: The control panel juts out over the paper exit but stays about 1 cm behind the front face. To load paper the whole cassette slides out of the front (about 30 cm).

Original TN-2510XL (3,000 pages, ₪398 at HD Toner) plus drum DR-2510 (15,000 pages, ₪456 at Beit HaFax).
With a compatible cartridge: ₪0.070 per page, TN-2510 (1,200 pages, ₪48 at PENPALL).

No report found about this model rejecting third-party toner. Brother's Australian FAQ says a non-genuine cartridge should go to its maker or seller, and mentions no chip or firmware rule. Chip-equipped compatibles are sold in the UK and Europe, and Brother has denied in press reports that firmware blocks third-party toner, but the research could not read that article in full.

Brother's own Windows 11 FAQs describe USB scanning failures and driver-install errors for this model, and a sibling's wireless scanning broke after a Windows 11 update with no confirmed fix, while owners of the US sibling DCP-L2640DW praise its scanning and Wi-Fi setup.

more.label: Driver
more.p: Brother's Full Driver & Software Package, which Brother's Windows 11 FAQs say to download from the model's Downloads page; the Brother EU Downloads page for this model rendered with no file list, so the version and size were not verified. Whether Windows Update installs a built-in driver was not verified.

more.label: App required
more.p: optional

more.label: Known problems
items: USB scanning on Windows 11: scan button does not work and the machine may not appear as a scanner (Brother's fix: remove the software, turn off Windows Ready Print and protected print mode, reinstall the Full Driver; Brother recommends a network connection instead)
Network scan blocked by firewall (fixed by allowing iPrint&Scan.exe and iPSNotifier.exe on Windows, or UDP port 54925 per Brother)
Computer name not shown on the machine's LCD, so scans cannot be sent to the PC (fixed by Brother's repair tool)
Wi-Fi drops (fixed by Recover WLAN on the panel, per Brother's Online User's Guide)
Driver install errors and printing failures on Windows 11 (Brother FAQ titles; the fix text was not read, no fix confirmed)
Sibling DCP-L2550DW: wireless scanning stopped after a Windows 11 update, printing still worked; no confirmed fix in the thread (sibling model, not this one)

more.label: Scanning
more.p: Flatbed (CIS) scanner with no document feeder. On Windows, Brother's FAQs route network scanning through Brother iPrint&Scan (iPrint&Scan.exe and iPSNotifier.exe handle the scan button, and the firewall must allow them). Brother's Windows 11 FAQ says USB scanning is unreliable, so use a network connection. Brother's FAQs for the sibling DCP-L2520DW say to set the Brother TWAIN or WIA driver as the primary source in scanning apps; that is not confirmed for this model. The Windows Scan app was not verified for this model.

A 10 out of 10 score from six LDLC reviews of this exact model and 4.3 out of 5 from 1,003 Walmart ratings for the US sibling DCP-L2640DW, with praise for easy setup and scanning and complaints about occasional Wi-Fi dropouts, sleep wake-up and toner cost.

No source found that says whether this printer rejects or nags about non-Brother TN-2510 cartridges, and no lock-out reports turned up. Compatible TN-2510 cartridges are sold in Israel for this model. The Brother authentication whitepaper the research saw covers inkjet cartridges only.

more.p: No Pantum page the research opened says whether the BP2300 family blocks non-genuine toner. Pantum's product page only links to a general 'Consumables Anti-Counterfeiting Identification' page. Compatible toner is sold in Israel, so the cartridge can be replaced by a third party, but whether the printer accepts it is unverified.

The BP2300NW and its relatives install driverless on Windows 8.1 to 11, but the rating rests on the maker page and three press reviews of the BP2300W, with no owner report on Windows found in this pass; reviewers describe a fiddly USB-first Wi-Fi setup.

more.label: Driver
more.p: Windows 10 and 11 install it without a manual driver (driverless, the driver installs on first connection, per the Inforeco and Adam Lobo pages). Pantum's own BP2300NW page offers a one-step driver download with Windows 11 32/64-bit listed. Adam Lobo reports that a CD driver is included. The Pantum driver download page itself was not opened. Third-party driver databases (Treexy) list BP2300W and BP2300NW IPP entries, but they are not the maker's site and were not used.

more.p: optional

items: Setup on Windows goes over USB first, and Wi-Fi is configured afterwards (pokde review of the BP2300W: 'a bit of puzzle solving'; no fix found in the reviews)

Retailer pages for this printer say its dynamic security blocks cartridges with a non-HP chip and that it is meant to work only with new or reused HP chips. Israeli sellers still list compatible 142A cartridges for it at 80 to 330 ILS; whether a given one works is untested, and the castleink page warns that firmware updates are more likely to block non-HP toner.

Owners on Windows 10 and 11 print fine once set up, either with HP's app, HP's full software, or the built-in Windows driver over USB, but Wi-Fi setup, offline status and app detection failures recur and several threads end with no confirmed fix.

more.p: No report found that firmware blocks third-party toner on the B230 itself. A Xerox B235 service manual (sibling model on the same platform) describes a 'non-Xerox supply detected' warning that can be bypassed by a key sequence; this is a search excerpt, not a page the research could open. One Xerox.ca owner blames a chip for blocking cheaper cartridges (single anecdote).

Xerox publishes Windows 10 and 11 drivers and the built-in IPP driver works, but owners and one reviewer report Wi-Fi setup trouble on the small screen and a setup failure with Xerox's recommended print system; the Xerox Support Community (the place where Windows setup threads would be) is behind a login, so no thread was read.
